checkpoints: After each edit, verify no store write occurs before the 120 ms trailing-task callback runs unless the trailing task is explicitly flushed by existing behavior.
At the end of a 120 ms quiet interval, verify exactly one write occurs for that burst and contains the latest submitted text.
After one burst saves, verify a later burst schedules and completes another save.
Verify navigating, closing, or changing the current badge does not discard a document buffer or its pending save.
Verify the search preview retains its existing 40 ms trailing behavior and cancellation on hide.
Verify public Java sources still compile under the supplied OpenJDK 11 runtime, with build outputs outside the workspace.
forbidden_effects: Do not write document edits to the store immediately on every call to edit.
Do not save intermediate text superseded within the same 120 ms editing burst.
Do not cancel or destroy a document buffer merely because its current Badge is detached, another document is opened, or the workspace view is closed.
Do not make Badge own document-buffer lifetime; Badge owns only its live store subscription.
Do not change search-preview timing, query payloads, or hide cancellation behavior.
Do not change public interfaces, source identities/text, status payload semantics, document payload semantics, or synchronous store/listener behavior.
Do not edit tests or configuration, and do not place compiled classes, binaries, or caches in the submitted workspace.
lifecycle_identity: Each document id has a persistent trailing buffer supplied by BufferBank and reused by later edits or views of that same id.
The current Badge represents only the live view/subscription for its document id and is detached when that view retires.
Pending document-save work belongs to the document buffer, independently of the current Badge.
Preview owns a separate transient trailing task with its own 40 ms quiet interval.

obligations.text: Workspace.edit must submit the current document's text to its existing per-document Trailing buffer instead of writing immediately.
The per-document trailing task must use a 120 ms delay and, after 120 ms without another edit in that burst, write only the latest text for that document.
Every newer edit within the quiet interval must replace the pending text and reschedule the trailing callback so intermediate values are not written.
After a trailing save completes, later editing bursts must be able to schedule and complete further saves.
Document buffers and pending document saves must remain owned by BufferBank independently of current Badge/view retirement, navigation, close, and Badge subscription detachment.
A completed save must retain existing synchronous write/listener/status behavior, including safety when a save callback synchronously navigates.
Workspace open, close, dispose, document output, store event, identity/text, and public API semantics other than edit coalescing must remain unchanged.
Search Preview must remain outside the change, retaining its distinct 40 ms trailing task and hide cancellation behavior.

ordering_barriers: For a burst, accept the newest edit and cancel the previously scheduled handle before scheduling the new 120 ms callback.
Do not invoke the document write until the trailing callback runs after the quiet interval.
When the trailing callback runs, clear its pending handle/text state as the existing Trailing utility specifies, then invoke the save work with the captured latest text.
Store write updates the record and revision before synchronously notifying subscribed listeners.
Retire detaches the old Badge subscription and emits the existing null document output; it must not cancel the BufferBank entry or its pending timer.
A synchronous navigation during save may retire or replace the Badge before the write call returns; no save logic may subsequently restore or act through the retired Badge.
preservation: Preserve `createWorkspace` operations open(id), edit(text), close(), and dispose().
Preserve current open/retire generation behavior and document outputs, including the document value read from the store on open.
Preserve store read/write/subscribe synchronicity and existing event/status payload semantics.
Preserve Badge filtering by document id and detachment of its live subscription on retirement.
Preserve per-document BufferBank identity across view changes.
Preserve Preview query(text), hide(), its 40 ms interval, and its `{query: q}` preview output.
Preserve all source identities/text and public interfaces except for the specifically requested delayed/coalesced save timing.

supporting_evidence.quote:
The workspace draft editor currently writes to the store on every keystroke.
Coalesce edits using the existing trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet
interval, write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts
must continue to save. Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces.
The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change.

A workspace document buffer persists independently of the current view badge. Save callbacks can synchronously navigate. Preview is transient and owns a different quiet interval. Document-buffer responsibility: separate BufferBank service

createWorkspace offers open(id), edit(text), close(), dispose(); createSearchPreview offers query(text), hide(). Store read/write/subscribe is synchronous; timer schedule(callback,delay), cancel(handle) is explicitly controlled.

Document buffers are owned by a separate BufferBank service, while Badge owns only a live subscription. A store listener may call navigation synchronously. All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics.

void push(String text) { if(handle!=null)env.cancel(handle); pending=text; handle=env.schedule(this::flush,delay); }
        void flush() { if(handle!=null)env.cancel(handle); String text=pending; handle=null;pending=null; if(text!=null)work.accept(text); }

static final class Badge {final String id;final Trailing buffer;final Environment env;final int token;Badge(Environment env,String id,Trailing buffer){this.env=env;this.id=id;this.buffer=buffer;token=env.store().subscribe(e->{if(id.equals(e.get("id")))env.output("status",e);});}void detach(){env.store().stop(token);}}

static final class BufferBank {final Map<String,Trailing> entries=new HashMap<>();Trailing get(Environment env,String id){return entries.computeIfAbsent(id,k->new Trailing(env,120,text->env.write(k,text)));}}
void edit(String text){Badge view=current;if(view!=null){env.write(view.id,text);}}

static final class Preview {final Trailing task;Preview(Environment env){task=new Trailing(env,40,q->{Map<String,Object>v=new LinkedHashMap<>();v.put("query",q);env.output("preview",v);});}void query(String text){task.push(text);}void hide(){task.cancel();}}

triggers: Calling Workspace.edit(text) while a Badge is current starts or refreshes that document's 120 ms trailing-save interval.
Another edit for the same current document before the timer fires cancels the old scheduled handle and replaces the pending text.
Expiration of the 120 ms quiet interval invokes one save with the latest pending text.
A later edit after a completed save begins a new burst and schedules a new save.
Opening, closing, disposing, or synchronously navigating retires the current Badge but does not itself cancel the separately owned document buffer.
Calling Preview.hide() cancels only the preview's pending task.

The public sources do not define concurrency or thread-safety requirements beyond synchronous store operations and explicitly controlled timers.

The public implementation still performs `env.write(view.id,text)` directly in `Workspace.edit`, contrary to the explicit requirement to coalesce edits through the existing trailing-task utility. Therefore the gap is localized to the edit path. The failed acceptance verdict supplies no additional requirement or reliable failure cause, while the successful compile check establishes only syntax/build validity.
